Nithya Raman’s win in the Los Angeles mayoral race marked a milestone for the Democratic Socialists of America — but she may not be lefty enough for some members of the movement.

The Long Beach chapter of the DSA issued a lengthy statement Friday warning the mayor-elect needs to govern like a “true democratic socialist” — or “we’ll bring the fight to her.”

While Long Beach is its own city, the chapter says its jurisdiction extends into the southernmost parts of LA. The group claimed Raman owed her victory to the chapter and other DSA members.

“Her association with DSA gave voters the confidence to elect her to lead Los Angeles, because DSA’s name is now synonymous with a new kind of politics,” the chapter wrote.

Now, Raman owes it to the group to fully embrace the DSA priorities, including tenant protections, housing, non-police public safety and pro-labor commitments, the chapter wrote.

Members noted that they don’t exactly trust the mayor-elect to follow through on their policies.

“We have to be honest about another thing. Raman’s record on Palestine, policing and special interests has given us pause,” the chapter wrote. “What many voters don’t seem to realize is that Raman has shown reluctance to fully commit to DSA’s values.”

The Long Beach chapter blasted Raman for not doing enough to intervene in the city’s “economic support for a genocidal apartheid state” and for proposing reforms to the city’s mansion tax that the chapter views as too friendly to developers.

The most headline-grabbing issue has been Raman’s promise to replace LAPD Chief Jim McDonnell — misspelled by the chapter as “McDonald” its post — “who has notably collaborated with ICE,” the group wrote.

Since winning, Raman has softened her stance and signaled McDonnell may keep his job — “a major concern” for the DSA chapter.

“Our support for Raman comes with concerns,” the chapter wrote. “It’s a partnership built on accountability.”

While Raman is a member of the DSA, her relationship with the movement has not always been friendly.

A few days before the election, she retained her DSA endorsement by a single vote from the group after a bitter feud over her shifting stance on boycotting Israel.

The mayor-elect’s campaign has downplayed the idea that she owes her victory to the DSA, citing the support of other allies like labor unions.

“I just don’t want the interest in DSA to overshadow the real work that those partners did,” Ian Manheimer, her campaign manager, told the New York Times.

The California Post contacted Raman’s campaign for comment.
news.content:
بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. پیروزی نیتیا رامان در رقابت شهرداری لس آنجلس نقطه عطفی برای سوسیالیست های دموکرات آمریکا بود - اما ممکن است او برای برخی از اعضای جنبش به اندازه کافی چپ نباشد. بخش لانگ بیچ DSA روز جمعه بیانیه ای طولانی صادر کرد و هشدار داد که شهردار منتخب باید مانند یک "سوسیالیست واقعی" حکومت کند. در حالی که لانگ بیچ شهر خودش است، این بخش می گوید حوزه قضایی آن تا جنوبی ترین بخش های لس آنجلس گسترش می یابد. این گروه ادعا کرد که رامان پیروزی خود را مدیون بخش و دیگر اعضای DSA است. این فصل نوشت: «ارتباط او با DSA به رای دهندگان اعتماد به نفس داد تا او را برای رهبری لس آنجلس انتخاب کنند، زیرا نام DSA اکنون مترادف با نوع جدیدی از سیاست است. اکنون، رامان این را مدیون این گروه است که به طور کامل از اولویت‌های DSA، از جمله حمایت از مستاجر، مسکن، امنیت عمومی غیرپلیسی و تعهدات حامی کارگری استقبال کند. اعضا خاطرنشان کردند که آنها دقیقاً به شهردار منتخب برای اجرای سیاست‌هایشان اعتماد ندارند. به نظر می رسد آنچه که بسیاری از رای دهندگان متوجه نمی شوند این است که رامان تمایلی به پایبندی کامل به ارزش های DSA نشان نداده است.
بخش لانگ بیچ رامان را به خاطر اینکه به اندازه کافی برای مداخله در "حمایت اقتصادی شهر از یک دولت آپارتاید نسل کشی" و پیشنهاد اصلاحات در مالیات عمارت شهر که به اندازه کافی انجام نداده، انتقاد کرد.

Taylor Frankie Paul, whose season of “The Bachelorette” was scrapped by ABC following a reported domestic violence incident involving her ex Dakota Mortensen, is jokingly throwing her hat in the ring for new “Bachelor” Sam Hartman’s upcoming season.

Following the announcement of Hartman, 27, as the next leading man of Season 30 of “The Bachelor,” Paul, 32, took to Instagram to hint that she may be interested in applying for a chance to receive his final rose.

In the Reel, Paul shared a scene from “Parks and Recreation” featuring Ron Swanson (Nick Offerman) typing on a computer. The screen displayed what appeared to be Paul’s application for the reality dating series.

When asked, “What do you think would make you stand out amongst the other ladies?” the application showed Paul’s response: “Ahhh, I was the first Bachelorette in history to be on hold.”

Swanson then proceeded to toss the computer into a dumpster. Paul captioned the video, “I chose to have the audacity 🌹.”

Paul also joined in on the conversation in the comments section of Bachelor Nation’s Instagram announcement, writing, “Dang, sign me up 😍.”

Hartman, a former quarterback for the Washington Commanders, was announced as the next “Bachelor” on Friday.

“I’m excited, but also very nervous,” he said during an appearance on “Good Morning America.” “I have a tough time holding a conversation with one girl. Thirty is going to be pretty tough.”

Meanwhile, Paul, best known for her appearance on “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives,” was announced as the lead of Season 22 of “The Bachelorette” last September.

However, ABC later pulled the plug on the season just days before its scheduled premiere following the release of a 2023 video showing Paul throwing metal barstools at Mortensen while her daughter, Indy, was in the room.

The network told Page Six in a statement, “In light of the newly released video just surfaced today, we have made the decision to not move forward with the new season of ‘The Bachelorette’ at this time, and our focus is on supporting the family.”

In March, a source told us that ABC could still potentially air the season, as the network reportedly faced losing between $50 million and $70 million if it chose not to move forward with the show.

“ABC left a window [open] in their statement to bring [the show] back. They haven’t canceled it — they simply paused it,” an industry insider said.

Paul, for her part, was still owed her low- to mid-six-figure salary, as she had fulfilled her contractual obligations by completing filming on the season.

Most recently, Paul announced that she was stepping away from “SLOMW,” citing “bullying” from her castmates and ongoing custody battles with the fathers of her children.

بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. تیلور فرانکی پل، که فصل "The Bachelorette" او توسط ABC به دنبال یک حادثه خشونت خانگی گزارش شده مربوط به داکوتا مورتنسن سابقش لغو شد، به شوخی کلاه خود را برای فصل آینده "لیسانسه" سام هارتمن در رینگ پرتاب می کند. پس از اعلام هارتمن، 27 ساله، به عنوان مرد اصلی بعدی فصل 30 سریال "لیسانس"، پل 32 ساله در اینستاگرام به این نکته اشاره کرد که ممکن است برای دریافت فرصتی برای دریافت آخرین گل رز خود علاقه مند باشد. در حلقه، پل صحنه ای از "پارک ها و تفریحات" را به اشتراک گذاشت که ران سوانسون (نیک آفران در حال تایپ کردن بر روی کامپیوتر) بود. صفحه نمایش چیزی است که به نظر می رسد برنامه پل برای مجموعه دوستیابی واقعیت باشد. وقتی از شما پرسیده شد: «فکر می‌کنید چه چیزی باعث می‌شود در بین سایر خانم‌ها متمایز شوید؟» برنامه پاسخ پل را نشان داد: "آههه، من اولین مجردی در تاریخ بودم که در حالت تعلیق بودم."
سوانسون سپس کامپیوتر را در یک زباله دان انداخت. پل این ویدیو را شرح داد: «من جسارت را انتخاب کردم.»
پل همچنین در بخش نظرات اعلامیه اینستاگرام Bachelor Nation به گفتگو پیوست و نوشت: "Dang, sign up me 😍." هارتمن، مدافع سابق فرماندهان واشنگتن، روز جمعه به عنوان "لیسانس" بعدی معرفی شد. او در جریان حضور در "صبح بخیر آمریکا" گفت: "من هیجان زده هستم، اما همچنین بسیار عصبی هستم." "من زمان زیادی برای گفتگو با یک دختر دارم. سی سالگی بسیار سخت خواهد بود."
در همین حال، پل، بی

news.originalContent:

Texas Roadhouse is expanding its Chicken Alfredo Pasta rollout and testing new nonalcoholic drinks across its three restaurant brands, according to a report.

The steakhouse chain added Chicken Alfredo Pasta to more than 600 locations in recent months and plans to bring it to the roughly 100 remaining locations by spring 2027, executives said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nation’s Restaurant News reported.

Operators had asked for a new menu item, and early tests of the pasta proved popular with customers and staff, CEO Jerry Morgan said.

“It’s a great choice for somebody who wants something a little bit different,” Michael Bailen, vice president of investor relations for Texas Roadhouse, said.

The new dish features grilled chicken, bacon and creamy Parmesan cheese sauce over penne, served with a choice of one side, the company told Fox News Digital.

Some fans praised the dish, with one woman on Facebook saying it was “so good” and that she hoped it would remain on the menu permanently.

Others, however, wondered what a pasta dish was doing on a steakhouse menu.

“Who goes to a steakhouse and orders chicken Alfredo?” one Reddit user said in a thread dedicated to Texas Roadhouse.

Bailen said the dish is “probably not going to be one of our top 10 mix entrée items that we offer, but it rounds out the menu.”

Texas Roadhouse is also seeing continued demand for mocktails and dirty sodas, according to the report. The company is now testing “energizer” drinks at all three of its brands: Texas Roadhouse, Bubba’s 33 and Jaggers.

The menu moves come as the company works to maintain momentum after sales growth slowed late in the third quarter, according to Nation’s Restaurant News.

Executives attributed part of the slowdown to a viral social media hoax that falsely accused Texas Roadhouse and Logan’s Roadhouse employees of planning to tamper with Black customers’ food. The company investigated and concluded the claims were false.

Sales and traffic improved each week in October and continued to strengthen in early November, executives said.

Texas Roadhouse expects to open approximately 35 company-owned restaurants across its three brands in 2026, with another 35 planned for 2027.

“Maybe the recovery has taken a little bit longer than some would have expected, but our operators are out there busting their butts and they’ve doubled down on everything they’re doing,” Bailen said.

Passengers on a Southwest flight were treated to an impromptu in-flight concert from rock legends including Hoobastank, Simple Plan and The Used amid a nationwide ground stop.

The wild singalong happened Friday aboard a plane bound for Orlando from LAX after the Federal Aviation Administration announced the unprecedented move just before 4 p.m. ET to ground all flights — prompting a wave of cancellations that left thousands of travelers stranded.

The music legends were on their way to perform in Florida on Saturday and Sunday as part of the national Vans Warped Tour 2026 when the ground stop was announced.

The Southwest flight was part of a special fan experience, according to numerous videos posted online.

In a slew of videos posted on social media, the rockers turned the travel nightmare into a rock show, belting out some of their biggest hits for fellow passengers.

The cabin transformed into a makeshift concert venue, with passengers holding up their phones as Hoobastank frontman Doug Robb walked down the aisle belting out songs including the band’s 2003 hit “The Reason,” while guitarist Dan Estrin strummed from the front of the plane.

In another clip from the tour’s official Instagram account, The Used frontman Bert McCracken rocked passengers with the band’s 2004 hit “All That I’ve Got” and 2002’s “The Taste of Ink.”

Simple Plan’s Pierre Bouvier kept it a bit more subdued, performing with his guitar at the front of the plane. Standing behind the mic, he performed several songs, including “I’m Just a Kid” and “Perfect” from the band’s 2002 debut album.

The plane was eventually able to take off, according to fan videos.

Although the freeze was lifted around 8:15 p.m. ET,  it was unclear how the ground stop would affect the weekend-long concert.

Vans Warped Tour founder Kevin Lyman posted a video message Saturday saying there were cancellations and schedule adjustments due to the grounding.

“We will have a few bands canceling and we will be updating you on that. Not as many as we thought, because the bands are working hard to change their flights,” Lyman said.

“Some bands have jumped in vans and [are] driving from as far away as Chicago and Houston.”

“We’re going to push some bands that were playing today, [they] will be playing on Sunday. We’ve extended the sets out and giving bands more time to play. Bear with us. We’re all working hard,” he added.

The Southwest flight was part of a fan experience, according to numerous videos posted online.

Those who were on board thanked the rockers for the show and said it really made a bad situation so much better.

“Thank you Southwest for the memories,” rocker Lolo wrote. “Every plane was grounded today, but the emo gods made sure this one flew.”

“Stuck on a plane for hours and you end up with a free Hoobastank show. Honestly not the worst way to wait it out,” another person added.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Saturday investigators were looking into whether a contractor’s error or a faulty router triggered the nationwide grounding.

As of Saturday, 4,467 flights across the US were canceled and another 4,430 were delayed, according to FlightAware data.

‘Tis the season to shop local, sip something festive and question why you thought you could squeeze one more shopping bag onto the subway.

In other words, NYC’s holiday markets are back.

They’re transforming plazas, parks and even department-store basements into winter wonderlands packed with handmade treasures, vintage finds, festive treats and plenty of opportunities to blow your holiday budget.

The classics are pulling out all the stops for 2026, with milestone anniversaries, boozy firsts and supersized shopping experiences, while unconventional pop-ups are offering alternatives to the usual ornaments and peppermint-scented candles.

Are you hunting for a one-of-a-kind gift, a little retail therapy or something decidedly stranger to put under the tree?

If so, The Post rounded up five NYC holiday markets worth adding to your seasonal itinerary.

42nd Street and Sixth Avenue, Manhattan | Now–Jan. 3, 2027

Some traditions are worth keeping — and Bryant Park’s Winter Village is celebrating a particularly big one this year: its 25th anniversary.

The Midtown favorite is back, transforming the park into a European-style holiday village with more than 180 kiosks hawking everything from handmade treasures to seasonal treats. Browse weekdays from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. and weekends from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.

New this season is a rotating spotlight on small businesses, alongside fresh food options like 12 Chairs Shuk, serving up Middle Eastern pita and hummus bowls.

But the biggest news may be for anyone looking to upgrade their annual Santa photo.

The new Club Santa VIP experience bundles premium skating access, holiday crafts and time with the big man himself inside the heated Polar Lounge on select dates, Nov. 28–29 and Dec. 5–6. There’s also a free, walk-up Santa’s Corner photo and wish-list station from Dec. 14–18.

Of course, the 17,000-square-foot ice rink remains the centerpiece, with free admission for those bringing their own skates (timed reservations required).

The rink and rinkside food hall will stick around through Feb. 28, 2027, long after the holiday shops pack up.

And for those who prefer their winter wonderland with a little more privacy, the heated Cozy Igloos are returning for private group reservations.

The tree lighting is scheduled for Dec. 2 at 5:30 p.m. — because no Manhattan holiday season is complete without a little extra sparkle.

Union Square Park, Manhattan | Now–Dec. 24, 2026

Union Square’s beloved holiday market has been a New York winter staple for years, but this season comes with a decidedly adult upgrade: For the first time in its history, shoppers can purchase beer and wine on-site.

That’s right — holiday shopping just got a little more spirited. The market is open Sunday through Wednesday from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m., Thursday and Friday until 9 p.m., and Saturdays from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m.

The city’s oldest, longest-running and largest open-air seasonal street market is returning with nearly 200 vendors, including a fresh crop of local makers and rotating small businesses.

Among the newcomers is The MB Edit, where former fashion editor Marybeth Schmitt is offering vintage fashion finds, as well as limited-edition NYC Parks merchandise for anyone who wants to rep their favorite green space.

A rotating Made in NYC booth will also spotlight six local small businesses throughout the season.

The weekly vendor lineup offers another reason to keep coming back. Silly Sketched Pets will be on hand with live pet portraits through Nov. 18, followed by Kettle & Kame Clay Studio’s pottery and ceramic jewelry from Nov. 19–25. Taiwanese-American bakery Rose’s Pineapple Shorts will bring its pineapple desserts to the market Nov. 27–Dec. 3.

Consider it a one-stop shop for holiday gifts, local discoveries and a little liquid cheer.

Macy’s Herald Square, 151 W. 34th St., Manhattan | Now–Jan. 3, 2027

Forget squeezing through a crowded sidewalk stall: Macy’s is bringing the holiday market indoors — and going big.

The department store’s Holiday Square has expanded to a whopping 50,000 square feet on the lower level of its iconic Herald Square flagship, transforming the basement into a festive shopping destination with more than 35 local artisans, gift makers and food vendors.

Shoppers can browse custom charm bracelets, cozy winter accessories, wreaths, floral arrangements, vintage parade apparel, stationery and books, or fuel up with treats from NYC favorites including Levain Bakery, Eataly, Pearl River Mart and Doughnut Plant.

There’s even a mini Museum of Ice Cream pink sprinkle-pool experience for anyone whose idea of holiday cheer involves a little sugar rush.

The indoor setting is a welcome perk for shoppers who’d rather stay warm and dry while checking off their gift lists. It’s open Monday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–9 p.m., and Sunday, 11 a.m.–9 p.m.

The festivities extend beyond the market, too. Macy’s Santaland opens Nov. 27, with reservations available beginning Nov. 20 on a rolling seven-day basis.

If fresh air is more your thing, Macy’s is bringing the holiday cheer outdoors, too. Its Urbanspace-run market in Herald and Greeley squares opens Dec. 3 and runs through Jan. 2, 2027, with vendor stalls, a double-decker carousel and a snow slide to keep shoppers entertained between purchases.

Add the store’s iconic holiday windows and the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, and Herald Square is worth the holiday pilgrimage.

Best of all, admission to Holiday Square is free — although your shopping bags, naturally, won’t be.

Metropolitan Pavilion, 125 W. 18th St., Manhattan | Saturday, Dec. 12, 2026

Not everyone wants a snow globe or a monogrammed mug for Christmas. For those whose holiday wish lists skew more Wednesday Addams than Martha Stewart, there’s the Oddities Flea Market.

The macabre marketplace is back for a one-day holiday edition, with more than 60 vendors peddling the wonderfully weird.

VIPs get first dibs from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m., while general admission runs from 1 to 6 p.m. Tickets cost $28.52 for general admission and $55.20 for VIP through Eventbrite, including a $5.20 fee.

Expect taxidermy, bones, anatomical curiosities, medical-history ephemera, insect jewelry, vintage treasures, dark art, flash tattoos and piercings and other curiosities that might make your more traditional relatives raise an eyebrow.

Founded in 2017 by osteologist and collector Ryan Matthew Cohn and Regina Marie Cohn, the market has carved out a niche for shoppers looking for gifts that are anything but cookie-cutter.

There are also custom flash tattoos and plenty of unusual collectibles to browse, making this less of a conventional shopping trip and more of an immersive experience.

DUMBO Archway and Plaza, Adams and Water streets, Brooklyn | Nov. 14–Dec. 20

Manhattan may get much of the holiday-market glory, but Brooklyn is bringing its own festive flair to the season on Saturdays and Sundays from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The Brooklyn Flea Holiday Market is setting up beneath DUMBO’s historic stone archway, with the Manhattan Bridge providing a particularly enviable backdrop for a little seasonal retail therapy.

The weekend market will feature roughly 40 to 50-plus curated vendors selling vintage clothing, antiques, handmade jewelry, ceramics, artwork, crafts and specialty foods — a particularly good hunting ground for shoppers who’d rather give something with a little history than another mass-produced stocking stuffer.

The final four weekends, Nov. 28 through Dec. 20, will bring an expanded holiday maker showcase featuring independent brands, jewelers, ceramists, artists and vintage collectors.

But the surrounding neighborhood is getting its own festive makeover, too.

New this year is a 25-foot live evergreen tree decorated with custom ornaments by artist Katie Wendt of Augenblick Studios, alongside brand-new animated video projections lighting up DUMBO.

The market will also serve as the pickup point for maps to Shop the Studios on Dec. 5, when more than 85 local artists open their workspaces to visitors.

And shoppers can take advantage of the free digital DUMBO Holiday Pass, running Nov. 15–Dec. 31, with deals at more than 50 neighborhood businesses, restaurants and shops.

It’s a holiday shopping trip with a distinctly Brooklyn twist — and a pretty spectacular photo op to boot.

Chaos continued Saturday at airports in the wake of the nationwide ground stop that brought all air travel in the US to a halt — with more than 4,000 flight delays and just as many flight cancellations stranding travelers across the country.

Though the FAA’s ground stop was lifted at 8:15 p.m., after four hours Friday, there were at least 4,467 cancellations across the US by Saturday afternoon, with another 4,430 delays.

Hundreds of stranded travelers camped out at New York’s LaGuardia and John F. Kennedy International airports and Newark Airport in New Jersey had their eyes glued to the airline boards in the unlikely hopes that they would soon be able to get to their destinations.

Clara Berdasco was approaching her 22nd hour in JFK’s Terminal 4 Saturday afternoon and was fearful that her second flight to Argentina could be canceled.

She was meant to fly out Friday to celebrate her 40th birthday with family — but the ground order was issued just two minutes before her flight was supposed to board.

“This is super wrong. Super, super wrong. We don’t know where we’re going to get food. It’s crazy how this happened. Of course it’s super bad for me, because I had a special occasion,” Berdasco said.

The birthday girl had 60 people coming to her bash, which she will now only make by the skin of her teeth, so long as her Sunday morning flight isn’t canceled, as her original one had been.

LATAM Airlines warned her that her flight wouldn’t be rescheduled a second time.

“I am kind of desperate. We had planned to have barbecue for 60 people and you can’t store meat for several days. They had already prepared all the food. We are from a country with a family that’s not rich,” said Berdasco, adding that her family was considering donating the party meal to a local church.

JFK reported 280 cancellations and 202 delays on Saturday, FlightAware data shows.

LaGuardia Airport had 193 cancellations and 189 delays, while Newark reported 223 canceled and 167 delayed flights.

The chaos led Franklin Daley, 35, to miss his cousin’s funeral in Jamaica — a service for which he was supposed to deliver a speech.

“I’m not feeling good about that. I’m actually disappointed. We were close. I used to help take care of him when he was a baby. And I’m stuck here. I have no option,” he said in anger.

Daley had been at JFK since 4 a.m. Saturday and was meant to fly out at 8 a.m., but his flight kept getting pushed back until it was rebooked for Monday.

The farmhand, who is working as a temporary apple picker in Hudson, plans to sleep at the airport until then because he cannot afford to stay at a hotel.

“The money that I have, I can’t even spare $100 out of it. I have to get a new roof for my house and take care of my two children,” Daley said.

“I will have dinner because I need real food but I’m going to skip breakfast, lunch and snacks.  I can’t afford it.”

Many travelers said they were forced to spend the night at the airport because nearby hotels jacked up prices. As of Saturday, rates at transit hotels in New York had reached as high as $550 for one night, The Post found.

The airlines are not offering vouchers for hotels since the decision to ground flights came from the government.

“The government has to be answerable to the people,” one Canadian passenger, who declined to share their name, told The Post.

“It’s disgusting. People were just camping on the floor all night. There are birds flying everywhere. It’s definitely been very frustrating. The worst part is that the airlines themselves are not very helpful.”

Maritza Cortez, 37, has been stranded in the airport since 4 p.m. Friday, telling The Post she has no idea when she’ll be able to make it home to Chile.

“They gave us boarding passes. We were at the gate and two minutes before we were supposed to get on the flight, they said it was canceled,” she said.

She has since bonded with Daniel Flores Gomez and his diabetic father, who were also meant to be on the same flight.

The men spent the night sleeping at JFK’s Terminal 4 after getting caught during their layover flight home to Chile after a 10-day trip in China.

“I keep asking LATAM, ‘When is the flight?’ They said they don’t know. They said 2 hours, 4 hours, 6 hours, tomorrow, it could be Monday. Tell me the truth!” Gomez told The Post.

“I’ve been sleeping here because I don’t want to leave and miss the first flight out. The floor is hard. I want to take a shower.”

His father, Pedro Flores Novoa, 66, is struggling with eating well in the airport, considering his condition.

“I’m tired and ready to go home — today, right now,” he said.

A young Kentucky couple thought they’d found their dream home — only to discover they’d moved into a slithering house of horrors crawling with dozens of snakes, some a staggering six feet long.

And the worst part — the army of scaly squatters may have been there for decades.

Jessica and Johnathan Perry had done everything by the book, including getting their new Mercer County home inspected before moving in, the couple told WKYT.

But just three weeks after unpacking, their American dream turned into a reptilian nightmare.

“I was actually taking out the trash,” Jessica said. “My son and I were home alone, and I walked out the door, and there was a snake on the porch.”

“I immediately called my husband and then my dad to come out here to get it. Then a few days later, we found another. And a few days later, another.”

Before long, the rat snakes were turning up everywhere, Jessica told FOX 56 News.

“Then one night, about a week after finding the first one, [Johnathan] and his friends came down in the basement and found two adults and several juveniles in the basement … that’s an infestation.”

And they weren’t just passing through.

Hoping to get to the bottom of their creepy home invasion, the couple hired a contractor to rip up the concrete floor of their front porch.

What they found was enough to make anyone’s skin crawl.

“When they busted through the middle, there were dozens and dozens of snake eggs, new and what looked like several years old.”

Then came an even bigger bombshell.

Apparently, the house’s reputation had been slinking around the neighborhood for years.

Jessica tracked down a former owner, who revealed that when he was a child, the property had a nickname: “The Snake House.”

Although the rat snakes aren’t venomous, the couple isn’t taking chances with their 5-year-old son.

“Not necessarily that we’d be scared they’d bite him,” Johnathan told WKYT. “Snakes like warmth. So, if they were to get in the upper level and get in the bed or whatever, they could curl up around his neck, per se.”

Now, instead of kicking back and enjoying their new home, the couple spends evenings on snake patrol.

“We ask each other, ‘Have you gone to the basement yet to check for snakes?'” Johnathan added.

And the nightmare is getting expensive.

A friend of the family has launched a GoFundMe to help cover the thousands of dollars the Perrys are shelling out to evict their unwanted reptilian roommates.

But the truly terrifying possibility isn’t how much dough it’s going to take to get rid of the home invaders — it’s that the infestation may be impossible to eliminate without demolishing the house.

“Now that we have found that it’s a decades-old problem, what worries us now is that there are multiple dens within the foundation of the home,” said Jessica.

“And in order to eradicate and mitigate that, you essentially bust down the entire home.”

جسیکا به FOX 56 News گفت، طولی نکشید که مارهای موش در همه جا ظاهر شدند. «سپس یک شب، حدود یک هفته پس از پیدا کردن اولین مار، [جاناتان] و دوستانش در زیرزمین پایین آمدند و دو بزرگسال و چند نوجوان را در زیرزمین پیدا کردند ... این یک هجوم است.» و آن‌ها فقط در حال عبور نبودند. این زوج به امید رسیدن به پایان حمله به خانه‌شان، پیمانکاری را استخدام کردند تا کف بتنی ایوان جلوی خانه‌شان را پاره کند. آنچه پیدا کردند برای خزیدن پوست هر کسی کافی بود. «وقتی از وسط شکستند، ده‌ها و ده‌ها تخم مار وجود داشت، تازه و چه لوبی.

news.originalContent:
Protesters chanted against declining affordability, the Macron government, police violence and poor school conditions.

More than 100,000 people have taken to the streets in France in another round of cost-of-living rallies organised by the “Yellow Vests” and various youth movements.

Saturday’s protests saw a decline in turnout compared with previous weekends and stayed largely calm, authorities said.

The Ministry of the Interior reported that 106,000 people took part in protests nationwide, including 24,000 in Paris – down from 146,000 people nationwide and 46,000 in Paris last week. Student unions place Saturday’s protest numbers higher, at 200,000 people, including almost 100,000 in the capital.

The country has been gripped by high-school blockades, mass demonstrations, and strikes for more than a month, with protesters rallying against falling educational standards, cost-of-living increases, low wages, and police violence.

A number of demonstrators also carried signs targeting President Emmanuel Macron, who has faced significant criticism from protesters.

Some rallies in recent weeks have seen violence at the fringes, and the first major protest on October 17 saw looting in cities across France. Since then, police presence at rallies and controls on transport and permits to protest have been expanded.

Marseille, France’s second-largest city, banned protests over the weekend, but the prefecture announced that some 3,500 people still took to the streets. Local media reported that tear gas and a water cannon were used against protesters and shared images of fires burning in a popular local square.

In Lyon, local media reported that roughly 8,000 people took to the streets. They shared images of masked protesters chanting in front of fires lit in the street and police charging and using tear gas.

Tear gas use was also reported in Nantes, Bordeaux and Paris.

Unions have called for a new day of strikes on Tuesday after rejecting a government promise to increase the minimum wage by 0.6 percent as “crumbs”.

If the demonstrations go ahead, they will take place on the eighth anniversary of the Gilet Jaune – which translates to “Yellow Vest” in French – movement, which rocked the beginning of the Macron government in 2018 with two years of protests triggered by rising fuel prices.

On Tuesday, the Yellow Vests will “celebrate their eight years where it all started: on roundabouts and toll booths all over France”, Yellow Vest protest tracking website 17octobregiletjaune.net writes.

news.originalContent:
These were the biggest protests against rising housing costs in Portugal since the social movement began weeks ago.

Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets of more than 30 towns and cities in Portugal to protest against surging rental prices, demanding urgent government action to address the country’s worsening housing crisis.

Organised by the Casa Para Viver (A Home to Live In) platform, demonstrations on Saturday took place under the slogan “They will not steal our right to a home,” with protests in Lisbon, Porto, Faro, Portimao, Coimbra, Braga and other locations. It was the biggest national demonstration since the social movement began weeks ago.

Participants, ranging from teenagers to retired people, walked behind large banners, with the Lisbon march punctuated by drums, music, and chanting. Protesters called for caps to be placed on rent increases, greater legal protection for tenants against eviction, and more affordable housing. They also demanded the reversal of proposed changes to rental legislation.

One woman on a protest march in Lisbon told Al Jazeera that she was a business owner, “and I can’t afford a house.”

“I can’t say much more than this. I’m forty-years-old, I can’t go to a bank and just buy a house with my money,” she added.

Another woman told Al Jazeera that she had joined the march to protest “for a better life, for all of us, not just the young people, all of us, because we deserve to have a home.”

One man told Al Jazeera “we have been suffering this for the last three or four years, and I have many friends and family in this situation, they had to move because they cannot afford the rent. If you earn, for example, a thousand euros, and you have to pay rent of six hundred, seven hundred, then you cannot live, it’s impossible.”

Casa Para Vivir brings together approximately 100 housing associations and grassroots organisations, is seeking tighter regulation on rental contracts, short-term tourist accommodation, and vacant properties.

The protests come after parliament approved the government’s proposed changes to provide greater flexibility in rental contracts and accelerate eviction procedures.

Housing campaigners warned the changes could weaken tenant protections amid rising rents and limited housing availability.

House prices in Portugal have risen much faster than incomes in recent years, statistics show. Between 2015 and 2025, Portugal posted the biggest jump in the European Union in the home price-to-income ratio, with an increase of 61 percent, followed by the Netherlands with 34 percent, the EU statistical office Eurostat said last week.

There is no indication that the rise in housing costs is slowing. Between the first quarter of last year and the first quarter of 2026, property prices rose by almost 20 percent, the National Statistics Institute, a government agency, said last month.

Rental prices, too, have climbed significantly, recording a 68 percent increase since 2020, according to the government. Much of this jump in real estate costs has been fuelled by foreign buyers and investment funds, as the country’s relaxed climate near the ocean has attracted many remote workers and retirees.

The government has responded to the protests by lowering taxes on new construction, restricting short-term rentals, and promising to build 145,000 new homes, but it acknowledged that the effects will not be immediate, as Prime Minister Luis Montenegro was urged by Casa Para Viver representatives to engage directly with them.

The protests in Portugal in recent weeks took their cue from demonstrations in neighbouring Spain last month over similar issues around housing and forced evictions. A wave of youth-led protests has swept Europe in the latter half of this year, with demonstrators across the continent denouncing rising prices and a lack of future prospects.

“We feel threatened by the uncertainty of widespread violence and by the unspeakable suffering that continues to afflict so many of our brothers and sisters, he said, speaking at his former cathedral in Chiclayo.

Peru’s homicide rate has nearly doubled over the past five years, from 5.8 to 10.7 per 100,000 people. Reported extortion cases rose from 2,421 in 2019 to 26,734 in 2025, according to official figures cited by The Associated Press.

Security was a top concern for Peruvians in the last election. Conservative President Keiko Jujimori took office in July after promising to tackle crime. She has since declared states of emergency, including in Lima in August, then in September in prisons holding inmates linked to criminal organisations.

She has also pursued closer ties with Washington, bringing Peru into the ‘Shield of the Americas,’ a US-led regional coalition formed to carry out joint military operations against drug cartels.

Later on Saturday, in the Andean town of Santa Cruz de Succhabamba with a population of about 6,000, about 20,000 people came to an outdoor Mass, where Leo also addressed violence in society.

“Selfishness, injustice and evil are not overcome by brutality, but by prayer, patience and perseverance in denouncing what is wrong, by making our pleas with determination and working diligently to bring about the necessary changes,” said the leader of the Roman Catholic church.

He also drew attention to the suffering of rural communities he used to serve, where migration and declining birth rates are emptying villages.

“Let us think, for example, of the suffering of those who are forced to leave their homeland in search of a better future for themselves and their families in the great coastal cities,” he said.

Originally from Chicago in the United States and formerly known as Robert Francis Prevost, Leo arrived in Santa Cruz de Succhabamba by helicopter and was welcomed by a local band singing “Pope Leo, welcome home.”

He’d made the journey to the remote area many times before during his time as bishop of Chiclayo from 2015 to 2023, driving himself along winding mountain roads in a pick-up truck.

The pope, who holds both US and Peruvian citizenship, spent about two decades working in Peru as a missionary priest and bishop.

news.originalSummary:

news.originalContent:
ایتالیا، شرکت متا، غول شبکه‌های اجتماعی، را به‌دلیل دسترسی به عکس‌های کاربران اندروید بدون دریافت رضایت صریح آنها، ۸۰۵ میلیون یورو (معادل ۸۸۷ میلیون دلار) جریمه کرده‌ است.

سازمان حفاظت از داده‌های ایتالیا اعلام کرده است که متا به حدود ۲۰ میلیون کاربر تلفن‌های هوشمند اطلاع‌رسانی مناسبی نکرده بود که از طریق یکی از قابلیت‌های اپلیکیشن فیسبوک به عکس‌ها و ویدیوهایشان دسترسی دارد.

این نهاد به متا دو ماه مهلت داده است تا این قابلیت را به‌طور پیش‌فرض غیرفعال کند و برای استفاده از آن، رضایت جداگانه کاربران را بگیرد.

این یکی از بزرگترین جریمه‌هایی است که تاکنون یک نهاد ایتالیایی علیه یک شرکت بزرگ فناوری اعمال کرده است.

موضوع این جریمه به قابلیتی مربوط می‌شود که عکس‌ها و ویدیوهای موجود در گالری تلفن همراه کاربران را به‌عنوان پیشنهادهایی برای انتشار پست در فیسبوک نمایش می‌دهد.

فیسبوک برای دسترسی به گالری عکس کاربران، فقط یک مجوز کلی در سطح اپلیکیشن درخواست می‌کرد.

به گفته نهاد ناظر ایتالیایی، اطلاعیه‌ای که پیش از آن به کاربران نمایش داده می‌شد، به‌روشنی توضیح نمی‌داد که این مجوز به فیسبوک اجازه می‌دهد بر اساس عکس‌های موجود در گالری تلفن همراه آنها هم پیشنهادهایی ارائه کند.

این نهاد اعلام کرد که در تعیین میزان جریمه، «تعداد زیاد افراد متأثر از این موضوع» و این واقعیت را در نظر گرفته است که این وضعیت «همچنان برای کاربرانی که اپلیکیشن خود را به‌روزرسانی نکرده‌اند و همچنین کسانی که پیشتر با این سازوکار موافقت کرده‌اند، ادامه دارد.»

نهاد ناظر ایتالیایی همچنین به «عدم همکاری متا» اشاره کرد. بی‌بی‌سی برای دریافت توضیحات در این باره با متا تماس گرفته است.

متا که همچون فیسبوک، شرکت مادر اینستاگرام و واتس‌اپ است ماه گذشته به‌دلیل شیوه‌های تجاری خود با بزرگترین جریمه تاریخ این شرکت روبه‌رو شد.

پس از آن که مشخص شد متا سال‌ها درباره نحوه مدیریت اطلاعات کاربران فیسبوک به افکار عمومی دروغ گفته، یک قاضی در ایالت نیومکزیکوی آمریکا این شرکت را به پرداخت ۲۵ میلیارد دلار  محکوم کرد.

news.originalContent:
Sean Duffy, the country’s transportation secretary, said his agency is ‘going to hold people accountable’.

The top United States transportation official has said work being performed on an antiquated telecommunications system could be to blame for a rare, hours-long US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that halted all air traffic inside the country.

At a news conference in Washington, DC, on Saturday, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy spoke about routine maintenance that was performed on Friday to upgrade a router from copper to fibre at a “very remote location”.

Duffy said “contractor error or a faulty piece of equipment” caused the router in question to start flooding other ones in the country’s air traffic control system.

“We had 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds,” he told reporters at the Department of Transportation.

When those connection issues caused disruption in radar feeds and communications between air traffic controllers and aeroplanes, Duffy said a ground stop was ordered.

“When we see that, your safety is paramount. We shut down the airspace,” he said.

The Transportation Department identified the contractor of Friday’s maintenance as L3Harris, a US-based aerospace and defence company that has been tasked with modernising the communications system for the FAA.

“What we’re working to determine was whether we had incompetence, meaning was it … installator error from L3Harris? Or did they install a faulty router?” Duffy said. “We haven’t determined what the fault was.”

Duffy added that L3Harris, which he said had performed decades of work for the FAA, “didn’t meet the moment”.

“They own this network. They’re our prime contractor. I can’t go somewhere else. They own it,” he said. “Or was it a faulty router? And we’re going to find that out. And frankly, we’re going to hold people accountable.”

In response to Duffy’s allegations, L3Harris told Al Jazeera it has been working “in close coordination with the FAA” and places safety and reliability as its “highest priorities”.

“We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the November 13 ground stop of our nation’s air travel,” a spokesperson for the company said. “L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travellers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously.”

Amid concerns that Friday’s ground stop was the result of a cyberattack, the US government said Saturday it did not “believe” that was the cause.

“Once we were able to isolate the work being done at this location, all of our systems came back online,” Duffy said. “So, we don’t believe this was cyber at all.”

The head of the FAA, who also spoke at Saturday’s news conference, echoed the transportation secretary’s remarks, saying the system outage was caused by an equipment error.

“We see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related,” FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said.

A root cause analysis would be shared with the public when it is available, he added.

As airlines and thousands of travellers begin the process of digging out from Friday’s groundstop, the longest and only second nationwide stop since 9/11, the FAA said full schedule integrity is expected by the end of Sunday.

“We have crews and aircraft that are out of position for 12,000 flights that were lost,” Bedford said. “These crews, pilots and flight attendants need to get to their points of reconnection with their schedules.”

Bedford said the FAA expects about 4,000 to 5,000 flights out of the 41,000 scheduled on Saturday to be cancelled.

“That will set us up for a full recovery tomorrow,” he said. “I do think the worst is behind us.”
news.content: شان دافی، وزیر حمل‌ونقل کشور، گفت آژانس او ​​«مردم را پاسخگو خواهد کرد». مقام ارشد حمل‌ونقل ایالات متحده گفته است که کارهایی که روی یک سیستم مخابراتی قدیمی انجام می‌شود می‌تواند مقصر توقف زمینی نادر و چند ساعته اداره هوانوردی فدرال آمریکا (FAA) باشد که تمام ترافیک هوایی در داخل کشور را متوقف کرد. در یک کنفرانس خبری در واشنگتن دی سی، روز شنبه، شان دافی، وزیر حمل و نقل ایالات متحده، در مورد تعمیر و نگهداری معمولی که در روز جمعه برای ارتقاء روتر از مسی به فیبر در "مکانی بسیار دور" انجام شد، گفت. او به خبرنگاران در وزارت حمل و نقل گفت: «ما 1000 تلاش برای اتصال در هر 4 تا 5 ثانیه داشتیم. وقتی این مشکلات اتصال باعث اختلال در تغذیه رادار و ارتباطات بین کنترل‌کننده‌های ترافیک هوایی و هواپیماها شد، دافی گفت دستور توقف زمینی داده شد. وقتی این را دیدیم، ایمنی شما بسیار مهم است. ما حریم هوایی را تعطیل کردیم.» وزارت حمل و نقل، پیمانکار تعمیر و نگهداری روز جمعه را L3Harris، یک شرکت هوافضا و دفاعی مستقر در ایالات متحده که وظیفه نوسازی سیستم ارتباطی FAA را بر عهده دارد، شناسایی کرد. news.originalContent:
منبع تصویر، AFP via Getty Images

ناوشکن آمریکایی «یو‌اس‌اس اسپروئنس» که در جریان جنگ آمریکا و اسرائیل علیه ایران ده‌ها موشک کروز تاماهاک شلیک کرده بود، پس از ۳۵۷ روز ماموریت به پایگاه خود در سن‌دیگو در ایالت کالیفرنیا بازگشت. به گفته نیروی دریایی آمریکا، این طولانی‌ترین ماموریت یک ناوشکن این کشور از زمان جنگ جهانی دوم بوده است.

نیروی دریایی آمریکا روز جمعه ۱۳ نوامبر اعلام کرد که ناوشکن اسپروئنس پس از نزدیک به یک سال حضور در ماموریت‌های دریایی و نظامی، به پایگاه خود بازگشته است.

این ناوشکن ۲۱ نوامبر ۲۰۲۵، در قالب گروه رزمی ناو هواپیمابر «آبراهام لینکلن»، سن‌دیگو را ترک کرد. ماموریت آن ابتدا برای حدود هفت ماه برنامه‌ریزی شده بود، اما با آغاز جنگ علیه ایران تمدید شد و حتی پس از بازگشت ناو هواپیمابر آبراهام لینکلن، اسپروئنس در خاورمیانه باقی ماند.

به گفته نیروی دریایی آمریکا، این ناوشکن در طول ماموریت خود بیش از ۸۸ هزار مایل دریایی پیمود و در جریان جنگ با ایران، ده‌ها موشک تاماهاک به سوی اهداف نظامی شلیک کرد.

مقام‌های آمریکایی همچنین می‌گویند که اسپروئنس در جریان عملیات نظامی، ۱۲ پهپاد و چهار موشک کروز ضدکشتی را سرنگون کرده است.

ناوشکن اسپروئنس از جمله شناورهای آمریکایی بود که در نخستین روز جنگ، ۲۸ فوریه، در حملات موشکی به ایران مشارکت داشت.

در همان روز، مدرسه ابتدایی شجره طیبه در شهر میناب در استان هرمزگان هدف حمله قرار گرفت. به گفته مقام‌های ایرانی، بیش از ۱۷۵ نفر، از جمله شمار زیادی کودک، در این حمله کشته شدند.

خبرگزاری آسوشیتدپرس در ماه مارس گزارش داد که ناوشکن اسپروئنس در محدوده برد موشکی مدرسه میناب قرار داشت و فرماندهی مرکزی ارتش آمریکا، سنتکام، تصویری از شلیک موشک تاماهاک از این ناوشکن در روز ۲۸ فوریه منتشر کرده بود.

با این حال، هنوز مشخص نشده است که آیا موشک اصابت‌کرده به مدرسه میناب از همین ناوشکن شلیک شده بود یا نه.

بخش راستی‌آزمایی بی‌بی‌سی با بررسی تصاویر ویدئویی تایید کرد که یک موشک تاماهاک آمریکایی به مجموعه نظامی سپاه پاسداران در مجاورت مدرسه برخورد کرده است. بررسی‌های گروه تحقیقاتی بلینگکت نیز نشان داد که حملات به این مجموعه و مدرسه احتمالا در دست‌کم دو موج انجام شده بود.

رویترز پیش‌تر به نقل از مقام‌های آمریکایی گزارش داده بود که یافته‌های اولیه تحقیقات ارتش آمریکا از احتمال مسئولیت نیروهای این کشور در حمله به مدرسه حکایت دارد.

هیئت حقیقت‌یاب سازمان ملل متحد نیز در ماه سپتامبر اعلام کرد که دلایل معقولی برای انتساب حمله به مدرسه میناب به نیروهای آمریکایی وجود دارد و شواهد موجود می‌تواند نشان‌دهنده ارتکاب جنایت جنگی باشد.

مقام‌های آمریکایی یافته‌های این هیئت را رد کرده‌اند. گزارش نهایی تحقیقات وزارت دفاع آمریکا درباره حمله به مدرسه نیز به‌طور عمومی منتشر نشده است.

منبع تصویر، Corbis via Getty Images

ناوشکن اسپروئنس علاوه بر حملات موشکی به ایران، در عملیات دفاع در برابر پهپادها و موشک‌های ایرانی و همچنین محاصره دریایی بنادر ایران مشارکت داشت.

این ناوشکن در ماه آوریل یک کشتی باری ایرانی به نام «توسکا» را که به گفته سنتکام از دستور نیروهای آمریکایی برای توقف پیروی نکرده بود، هدف تیراندازی قرار داد.

ماموریت طولانی اسپروئنس در حالی پایان یافته است که ادامه استقرار ناوهای آمریکایی در خاورمیانه نگرانی‌هایی درباره فشار بر خدمه، فرسودگی تجهیزات و دشواری نگهداری از شناورهای جنگی ایجاد کرده است.

بازگشت این ناوشکن به سن‌دیگو، پایان یکی از طولانی‌ترین ماموریت‌های دریایی آمریکا در دهه‌های اخیر است؛ ماموریتی که بخش مهمی از آن با جنگ علیه ایران و عملیات نظامی در خاورمیانه همراه بود.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by ROBERTO SCHMIDT / AFP via Getty Images)

Marco Rubio reached back more than 2,000 years to a Roman general to warn the International Criminal Court (ICC) that its rulings carry no force over Americans.

The secretary of state delivered the message during a keynote to the Federalist Society’s National Lawyers Convention in Washington Friday, according to a State Department transcript.

The same answer the Roman commander Pompey once gave to those citing their city’s charters against his legions would greet any move to enforce the court’s decrees on U.S. citizens, Rubio stated. “Stop quoting laws to men with swords,” he said. The line drew laughter, and he joked that the words were not politically correct.

FULL REMARKS: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Delivers Keynote Address, Answers Questions at Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention https://t.co/I9Zbat5ZVY

Rubio accused the court and its global-bureaucracy allies of making themselves “judge and jury and executioner of the international order” while answering to no one, according to the transcript. The tribunal now claims the power to investigate, prosecute and jail Americans under rules the country never approved, he stated. (RELATED: Trump Admin Announces Sanctions Against International Criminal Court Chief)

The secretary cast international law itself as a weapon of a global elite, arguing that critics had wielded it against nearly every major foreign policy decision of the Trump administration, Agence France-Presse (AFP) reported. He pointed to the U.S. military’s strikes on cartel boats in the Caribbean and the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro as moves that drew such objections, and he turned the same scorn on the United Nations.

The address was Rubio’s first major speech at home since Republicans absorbed heavy losses in this month’s midterm elections, and the crowd met him with a standing ovation, AFP reported. His choice of a prominent legal audience fed new speculation about a 2028 presidential bid, according to the Hill.

The appearance followed the sweeping sanctions the administration placed on the court in October as part of a campaign it says will dismantle the tribunal, the Associated Press (AP) reported. Washington signed the treaty that created the ICC yet never ratified it, which leaves the United States outside the court alongside Israel, Russia and China, AFP reported.

Enforcement is where the court runs thin, since it fields no police force and leans on member nations to arrest anyone it indicts, AP reported. The United States is not one of them.

Rubio tied the fight to national identity in closing. “To submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats would be to betray who we are, to betray ourselves,” he stated in the remarks.

مارکو روبیو بیش از 2000 سال پیش به یک ژنرال رومی مراجعه کرد تا به دادگاه کیفری بین‌المللی (ICC) هشدار دهد که احکام آن هیچ قدرتی بر آمریکایی‌ها ندارد. بر اساس رونوشت وزارت امور خارجه، وزیر امور خارجه این پیام را در جریان سخنرانی اصلی کنوانسیون ملی وکلای جامعه فدرالیست در روز جمعه در واشنگتن ارائه کرد. روبیو اظهار داشت که همان پاسخی که پومپیوس فرمانده رومی زمانی به کسانی که به منشورهای شهرشان علیه لژیون‌هایش استناد می‌کردند، از هر حرکتی برای اجرای احکام دادگاه در مورد شهروندان ایالات متحده استقبال می‌کرد. او گفت: «از ذکر قوانین برای مردان شمشیردار خودداری کنید. این خط باعث خنده شد و او به شوخی گفت که این کلمات از نظر سیاسی درست نیستند. اظهارات کامل: مارکو روبیو، وزیر امور خارجه، سخنرانی کلیدی، پاسخ به سؤالات در کنوانسیون ملی وکلای جامعه فدرالیست https://t.co/I9Zbat5ZVY
روبیو دادگاه و متحدان بوروکراسی جهانی آن را متهم کرد که خود را «قاضی، هیئت منصفه و مجری نظم بین‌الملل» می‌دانند در حالی که بر اساس متن به هیچ‌کس پاسخ نمی‌دادند. او گفت که دادگاه اکنون ادعا می کند که این قدرت را دارد که آمریکایی ها را تحت قوانینی که هرگز تصویب نکرده است، تحقیق، محاکمه و زندانی کند. (مرتبط: ادمین ترامپ علیه رئیس دیوان کیفری بین المللی تحریم ها را اعلام کرد)

news.originalContent:
At least 11 employees at two of America’s most powerful intelligence and cyber warfare agencies have died by suicide over the past year, prompting scrutiny from Congress and the White House.

The deaths occurred among military personnel, civilian employees and contractors working for the National Security Agency (NSA) and U.S. Cyber Command, including five suicides within roughly one month that military officials classified as a suicide cluster, according to The Japan Times. The deaths have prompted congressional inquiries and new restrictions on working hours as the agencies grapple with mounting operational demands from overseas conflicts, although officials have not determined that workplace pressures caused the suicides.

The Pentagon referred the Daily Caller News Foundation to Cyber Command who did not respond for comment. The NSA also did not respond to the DCNF’s request for comment. (RELATED: ‘Leadership Doesn’t Know Anything Else’: Why Are Suicide Rates In US Military So High?)

“The pace of operations right now at both NSA and Cyber Command can be overwhelming,” said Harry Coker Jr., a former senior executive at the NSA and Central Intelligence Agency told The Japan Times. “There is a lot of stress that a lot of us overlook because we think cyber is away from the front, and physically that’s accurate but intellectually and emotionally it’s inaccurate.”

Stallings’ family remembered him as as a devoted and discreet officer. He loved riding his motorcycle, reading Green Lantern comics and his chihuahua, Scud. As a kid, he covered his bedroom with glow-in-the-dark stars and stayed up late, reading under the blankets by flashlight. https://t.co/41wtOy924W

From early June to early July, five employees at the NSA and Cyber Command took their lives. These were categorized as cluster suicides, a phenomenon defined as when “suicides or suicide attempts happen closer together in time, location, or both than expected,” per the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The most recent suicide was in September.

This timeline of this cluster coincides with America shifting from a fragile ceasefire agreement with Iran to renewed fighting, according to United States Central Command (CENTCOM).

Even as legislators and military officials made efforts towards addressing the unique mental health challenges faced by these personnel, the suicides continued. Of the ten suicides, nine took place in Fort Meade, Maryland and one in Georgia, according to The Japan Times.

Congressional committees overseeing the military and intelligence agencies requested briefings from both agencies regarding the suicides and workload stress. Tim Kosiba, the NSA’s deputy director, went to the White House to brief officials, per the outlet.

NSA and Cyber Command leaders said that each servicemember had distinctly different motives for ending their lives including personal and financial issues. Technical Sergeant Kevin Stallings referred to a “wall of debt,” his divorce, an earlier suicide in his military unit and the death of his dog, Scud, for his June 11 suicide. Stallings apologized to his military leaders in his suicide note, saying they could not have prevented it.

“This is something I would never reach out for,” he wrote in the note obtained by The Japan Times.

Gen. Joshua Rudd, the Cyber Command and NSA leader, requested $11 million in April to address personnel mental health, warning of possible “burnout and force degradation.”

Two lawmakers sent letters urging the approval of this request in October, following the string of suicides per The Japan Times.

“While we know a lot about warfare,” Democratic Maryland Rep. Sarah Elfreth said according to Bloomberg. “[W]e don’t know much about electronic warfare in terms of its impact on the psyche and people’s mental health.”
news.content:
دست‌کم 11 کارمند در دو سازمان اطلاعاتی و جنگ سایبری قدرتمند آمریکا طی سال گذشته بر اثر خودکشی جان خود را از دست داده‌اند و این امر باعث بررسی دقیق کنگره و کاخ سفید شده است. این مرگ‌ها در میان پرسنل نظامی، کارمندان غیرنظامی و پیمانکارانی که برای آژانس امنیت ملی (NSA) و ایالات متحده کار می‌کردند، رخ داده است. به گزارش ژاپن تایمز، فرماندهی سایبری، شامل پنج مورد خودکشی در مدت تقریباً یک ماهه که مقامات نظامی آن را به عنوان یک خوشه انتحاری طبقه بندی کردند. این مرگ و میرها باعث تحقیقات کنگره و محدودیت‌های جدید در ساعات کاری شده است زیرا آژانس‌ها با تقاضاهای عملیاتی فزاینده ناشی از درگیری‌های خارج از کشور دست و پنجه نرم می‌کنند، اگرچه مقامات مشخص نکرده‌اند که فشارهای محل کار باعث خودکشی شده است. پنتاگون پایگاه خبری دیلی کالر را به فرماندهی سایبری ارجاع داد که برای اظهار نظر پاسخی نداد. NSA همچنین به درخواست DCNF برای اظهار نظر پاسخ نداد. (مرتبط: "رهبری چیز دیگری نمی داند": چرا میزان خودکشی در ارتش ایالات متحده بسیار بالا است؟)
هری کوکر جونیور گفت: "سرعت عملیات در حال حاضر هم در NSA و هم در فرماندهی سایبری می تواند بسیار زیاد باشد." یکی از مدیران ارشد سابق NSA و آژانس اطلاعات مرکزی به ژاپن تایمز گفت. استرس زیادی وجود دارد که بسیاری از ما آن را نادیده می گیریم زیرا فکر می کنیم سایبر از جبهه دور است و از نظر فیزیکی دقیق است اما از نظر فکری و احساسی نادرست است.

news.originalContent:
Shutterstock image via user Andrey Popov

Microsoft claimed early Saturday morning that the functionality of its Outlook email program has been restored for its 100 million users after a roughly 36-hour outage.

“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the Microsoft 365 Status account announced on X at 1:09 a.m. EST. The outage occurred at approximately 11:17 a.m. EST Thursday, affecting 74 countries and territories within an hour, according to Downdetector. (RELATED: Microsoft Says Email Backlog ‘Approaching Normal’ After Outage Paralyzes Outlook)

“We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners,” a Microsoft spokesperson told the Daily Caller News Foundation. “We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.”

We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions. Further updates can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 products, according to Microsoft’s fiscal year 2025 third-quarter earnings call.

Along with affecting health services in the United Kingdom, law enforcement in Australia, and tax transactions in Singapore, the outage also appears to have affected legislative operations in Congress as it begins its lame-duck session, The New York Times reported Friday.

“We have seen improvements to Outlook’s functionality this morning, but will continue to monitor the situation until all issues are resolved and full functionality is restored to all Microsoft applications,” House Chief Administrative Officer spokeswoman Samantha Carter told the outlet.

“We all use Outlook, that’s our life, everything is there, our calendar is there, our boss’s calendar, so it has been a challenge … with no access to our Bible,” one House staffer reportedly told POLITICO. “There goes a day of legislative work.”

While Microsoft confirmed the outage was not caused by a cyberattack, the company has faced Microsoft 365 outages in January, July, and August of 2026.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters late Friday that Microsoft’s latest outage and the Federal Aviation Administration’s recent nationwide ground stop are “separate issues.”

Microsoft stated Friday it will release an incident report of the outage. It also stated the problem was introduced “during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change.”

Editor’s note: This breaking news report was updated with a statement from Microsoft.
news.content:
تصویر Shutterstock از طریق کاربر Andrey Popov
مایکروسافت اوایل صبح شنبه ادعا کرد که عملکرد برنامه ایمیل Outlook آن برای 100 میلیون کاربرش پس از یک قطعی تقریباً 36 ساعته بازیابی شده است. حساب وضعیت Microsoft 365 در ساعت 1:09 a در ساعت 1:09 a اعلام کرد: «ما تلاش‌های خود را برای رسیدگی به مشکل اساسی این حادثه تکمیل کرده‌ایم و خدمات را به مشتریان و مناطق آسیب‌دیده بازیابی کردیم. به گزارش Downdetector، این قطعی تقریباً در ساعت 11:17 صبح پنجشنبه به وقت شرقی رخ داد و در عرض یک ساعت 74 کشور و منطقه را تحت تأثیر قرار داد. (مرتبط: مایکروسافت می‌گوید پس از قطع شدن ایمیل، پس از قطع، بک لاگ ایمیل به حالت عادی نزدیک می‌شود و Outlook را فلج می‌کند)
سخنگوی مایکروسافت به پایگاه خبری دیلی کالر گفت: «ما عمیقاً از اختلالی که این حادثه برای مشتریان و شرکای ما ایجاد کرده متأسفیم. ما از اعتماد آنها به خدمات ما آگاه هستیم و این مسئولیت را بسیار جدی می‌پذیریم. ما شاهد بهبود و ثبات گسترده در خدمات خود هستیم.»
ما تلاش‌های خود را برای رسیدگی به مشکل اساسی حادثه تکمیل کرده‌ایم و خدمات را به مشتریان و مناطق آسیب‌دیده باقی‌مانده بازیابی کرده‌ایم. به‌روزرسانی‌های بیشتر را می‌توانید در MO1550821 در مرکز مدیریت Microsoft 365 پیدا کنید. بر اساس فراخوان درآمد سه ماهه سوم سال مالی 2025 مایکروسافت، بیش از 430 میلیون نفر از محصولات مایکروسافت 365 استفاده می کنند. به نظر می رسد که این قطعی در کنار تأثیرگذاری بر خدمات بهداشتی در بریتانیا، اجرای قانون در استرالیا، و تراکنش های مالیاتی در سنگاپور نیز تأثیر گذاشته است.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Natalie Behring/Getty Images)

A federal power agency is weighing whether to join a California-operated electricity market, but most Westerners polled say their utilities should stay independent.

A draft decision on which day-ahead electricity market the Bonneville Power Administration will join is expected in December, Bonneville senior spokesperson Kevin Wingert said in a statement to the Daily Caller News Foundation. The agency had proposed in March to join a rival to the California market, Markets+.

Seventy-two percent of adults surveyed in five Western media markets said their local utility should stay “independently governed.” Just 10 percent would rather see it coordinate with a “California-run system,” the council’s slides show. The remaining 19 percent said they were not sure.

Causeway Solutions ran the poll for the Western Energy Markets Integrity Council. The advocacy group opposes putting Bonneville’s federal hydropower in what it called a “California-centric trading platform.”

“Pushing these federal assets into the hands of California will have profound adverse consequences for affordability and reliability of power in a region that can ill afford it,” the council said in an Oct. 22 statement to the DCNF.

“The council is an independent not-for-profit organization that receives contributions from power providers and consumers, and individuals. It coordinates with other public interest groups,” Scott Segal, a Bracewell LLP partner speaking for the council, said in a statement. His statement did not name any of those contributors.

“It’s good for California. It’s just bad for everybody else that joins with them,” H. Sterling Burnett, director of the Arthur B. Robinson Center on Climate and Environmental Policy at the Heartland Institute, told the DCNF in a Tuesday interview.

When the DCNF asked who would get power if the whole West ran short, Burnett said, “Well, the big dog eats first.”

He compared it to fights over the Colorado River, saying California gets the most water when there are shortages.

“They have the representatives in the House. They have the biggest population. They get it first,” Burnett said of California.

“California’s disastrous energy policies should serve as a warning to every Western state and no state should allow Sacramento to export its failures across state lines,” Oliver McPherson-Smith, vice chair for energy and environment policy at the America First Policy Institute, said in a statement to the DCNF.

“Customers in other Western states have good reason to resist putting their electricity bills and reliability under the influence of California politicians they didn’t elect and cannot hold accountable,” Jason Isaac, founder and CEO of the American Energy Institute, said in a statement. “Accountability should stay with the people who pay the bills.”

“The Department of Energy is committed to ensuring that American families and businesses, including those across the Pacific Northwest, have access to affordable, reliable, and secure electricity,” a department spokesperson said in a statement to the DCNF.

“Markets+ provides independent governance today,” the Southwest Power Pool, which would run Markets+, said in a statement. “More than one market in the West promotes choice and competition, which enables better outcomes for all participants and states.”

The California Independent System Operator did not respond to the DCNF’s request for comment. (RELATED: Data Center Boom Sparks Battle Over Power Costs, New Regulations)

Independence came out ahead in each market. Support ran from 64 percent in the Billings, Montana, area to 81 percent in the Tri-Cities of Washington.

Those two results carry margins of error of 4.7 points in Billings and 4.9 points in the Tri-Cities, per the slides.

Among the 1,733 people who picked a side, 88 percent chose independence and 12 percent favored coordinating with California.

Eighty-four percent of those surveyed were at least somewhat worried about their electric bills.

Causeway surveyed 2,095 adults, not registered voters, from Sept. 21 to 25 in the Boise, Idaho; Tri-Cities, Washington; Medford, Oregon; Gilbert and Mesa, Arizona; and Billings, Montana, media markets, the council’s polling page says. The text-to-web survey has an overall margin of error of 2.1 percentage points.

Bonneville’s March proposal set a target start date of Oct. 1, 2028, for Markets+. That came after a May 2025 Bonneville policy that put the agency on a path toward Markets+.

That plan is now under review. Bonneville Administrator and CEO Travis Kavulla wrote in a Sept. 3 letter that he had committed to reviewing that course “with fresh eyes.”

He would propose a change in Bonneville’s next draft decision if the agency sees “concrete actions” on governance of the California operator’s market, he wrote. Independent board leadership topped his list.

California revised its laws in 2025 so a separate regional body could govern that market with a board “appointed through an independent process rather than by state actors,” Kavulla noted.

That body, the Regional Organization for Western Energy, is set to interview candidates for its first CEO in December, RTO Insider reported Nov. 11.

“A more unified grid in the West with greater scale, market depth, and more contiguous corridors may alleviate operational and economic risks that would persist in a more fragmented market footprint,” Wingert, Bonneville’s senior spokesperson said. (RELATED: ‘Whole ’Nother Rent’: Soaring Electricity Prices In Kamala Harris’ Home State Are Crushing Residents)

Size is the draw. Leaving out Bonneville’s balancing area, the California operator’s market averaged 39 gigawatts of net generation, against 19 for Markets+. Kavulla cited federal Energy Information Administration data.

The Southwest Power Pool’s website lists an address in Little Rock, Arkansas.

Lawmakers from the Southwest Power Pool’s home state want Bonneville to stay the course. Republican Arkansas Sens. Tom Cotton and John Boozman wrote to Kavulla on Sept. 25 backing Bonneville’s “timely participation” in Markets+.

“The importance of independent governance cannot be overstated,” they wrote. The senators added that the California operator “is and remains statutorily beholden to the interests of the State of California.”

Western Montana’s electric co-op managers said in an Oct. 1 letter to Kavulla that their co-ops “strongly favor SPP.”

Advanced Energy United, which represents clean energy businesses, backed Bonneville’s review in September. The group’s senior director, Brian Turner, said the agency “recognizes the important strides that have been made around governance,” Utility Dive reported.

Bonneville has a workshop on its choice scheduled for Nov. 19, Wingert said.

Kavulla asked the regional body to adopt a framework that lets market participants “initiate and evaluate major market proposals,” with the end of November as his target.
news.content:
(عکس از ناتالی برینگ/گتی ایماژ)
یک آژانس برق فدرال در حال بررسی این است که آیا به بازار برق تحت مدیریت کالیفرنیا بپیوندد یا خیر، اما اکثر غربی‌های شرکت‌کننده در نظرسنجی می‌گویند که شرکت‌های برق آنها باید مستقل بمانند. کوین وینگرت، سخنگوی ارشد Bonneville در بیانیه‌ای به بنیاد Daily Caller News گفت: پیش‌نویس تصمیمی در مورد اینکه اداره برق Bonneville به کدام بازار برق روز آینده بپیوندد، در دسامبر انتظار می‌رود. این آژانس در ماه مارس پیشنهاد کرده بود که به رقیب بازار کالیفرنیا، Markets+ بپیوندد. هفتاد و دو درصد از بزرگسالان مورد بررسی در پنج بازار رسانه‌ای غربی گفتند که شرکت محلی آنها باید "به طور مستقل اداره شود." اسلایدهای شورا نشان می دهد که فقط 10 درصد ترجیح می دهند آن را با "سیستم مدیریت کالیفرنیا" هماهنگ کنند. 19 درصد باقی مانده گفتند که مطمئن نیستند. Causeway Solutions نظرسنجی را برای شورای یکپارچگی بازارهای انرژی غربی انجام داد. این گروه مدافع با قرار دادن نیروگاه آبی فدرال بونویل در آنچه که آن را «سکوی تجاری مرکزی کالیفرنیا» نامید، مخالف است.
این شورا در بیانیه ای در 22 اکتبر به DCNF گفت: "سپردن این دارایی های فدرال به دست کالیفرنیا پیامدهای نامطلوب عمیقی برای مقرون به صرفه بودن و قابلیت اطمینان قدرت در منطقه ای خواهد داشت که نمی تواند آن را بپردازد." اسکات سگال، شریک Bracewell LLP که برای شرکت صحبت می کند، "شورای یک سازمان غیر انتفاعی مستقل است که از ارائه دهندگان برق و مصرف کنندگان و افراد کمک می کند. این شورا با سایر گروه های منافع عمومی هماهنگ می شود."

news.originalContent:
ولودیمیر زلنسکی، رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین می‌گوید که مذاکره‌کنندگان آمریکایی پیشنهاد کرده‌اند که اوکراین در ازای عضویت در ناتو، نیروهای باقی‌مانده خود را از منطقه دونباس در شرق این کشور خارج کند.

اظهارات روز شنبه رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین در پی سفر نمایندگان ایالات متحده به مسکو و برگزاری نشست سران اتحادیه اروپا در دوبلین، پایتخت جمهوری ایرلند مطرح شد؛ اقداماتی که بخشی از تلاش‌ها برای پایان دادن به جنگ میان روسیه و اوکراین است.

اوکراین مدت‌هاست که عضویت در ناتو را به عنوان شرطی برای هرگونه توافق صلح، به‌منظور بازداشتن تهدیدهای آینده،  دنبال کرده است؛ این در حالی است که روسیه اعلام کرده حضور یک عضو دیگر این ائتلاف نظامی در مرزهایش غیرقابل‌قبول است.

ولودیمیر زلنسکی همواره گفته است که اوکراین حاضر نیست از قلمرو حاکمیتی خود دست بکشد؛ ولی مسکو خواستار واگذاری منطقه دونباس توسط اوکراین است.

آقای زلنسکی روز شنبه به خبرنگاران گفت: «آمریکایی‌ها این پرسش را مطرح کردند: 'اگر اوکراین به ناتو بپیوندد چه می‌شود؟ آیا اوکراین از دونباس عقب‌نشینی خواهد کرد؟' این نخستین باری بود که چنین موضوعی مطرح می‌شد.»

او در ادامه گفت که اگر پیشنهادی دریافت کند که شامل تضمین‌های امنیتی، اعمال نشدن محدودیت بر ارتش اوکراین و اختصاص بودجه برای بازسازی کشورش باشد، آن را به همه‌پرسی خواهد گذاشت.

جرد کوشنر و استیو ویتکاف، فرستادگان ایالات متحده، پس از یک دور گفت‌وگو با ولادیمیر پوتین، رئیس‌جمهور روسیه در مسکو، روز پنجشنبه برای دیدار با آقای زلنسکی به پایتخت جمهوری ایرلند سفر کردند.

اظهارات ولادیمیر پوتین و مقامات روسیه نشان می‌دهد که موضع روسیه در قبال جنگ تغییری نکرده است و خواسته‌های مسکو درباره تصاحب اراضی و بی‌طرفی، همچنان بسیار فراتر از آن چیزی است که اوکراین حاضر است آن را مدنظر قرار دهد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

روسیه پیش‌تر محدود کردن اندازه ارتش اوکراین، واگذاری‌های ارضی و تضمین بی‌طرفی کی‌یف را به عنوان شروط یک توافق صلح پیشنهاد کرده بود.

اوکراین این پیشنهادها را رد کرد و استدلال کرده است که چنین محدودیت‌هایی توانایی این کشور را برای دفع هرگونه تهاجم احتمالی در آینده، متاثر خواهد کرد.

با این حال، اخیرا نشانه‌هایی از یافتن زمینه‌ای مشترک میان طرفین پدیدار شده است.

ماه پیش، ملانیا ترامپ، بانوی اول ایالات متحده، توانست در منطقه خرسون میانجی‌گری کند تا آتش‌بسی موقت برقرار شود و امکان خارج کردن افراد و ارسال کمک‌ها فراهم شود.

مقامات آمریکایی پیش‌تر گفته بودند که عضویت اوکراین در ناتو منتفی است.

ولودیمیر زلنسکی روز شنبه گفت که پیشنهاد ایالات متحده باعث شده است باور کند که «ناتو دوباره در دستور کار قرار دارد.»

اما او هشدار داد: «شما هم سیگنال‌های پوتین را شنیده‌اید، و این گفت‌وگویی بسیار دشوار است.»

روسیه در حال حاضر حدود یک‌پنجم از خاک اوکراین، از جمله بخش عمده‌ای از مناطق دونتسک و لوهانسک را که منطقه دونباس را تشکیل می‌دهند، اشغال کرده است.

واگذاری بخش‌های کوچکی از اراضی که هنوز در کنترل اوکراین است، برای این کشور از نظر نمادین حائز اهمیت خواهد بود؛ چنین چیزی به منزله پذیرش این واقعیت است که منطقه دونباس به روسیه واگذار شده است.

آقای زلنسکی پیش‌تر درباره بازپس‌گیری قلمروهای تحت کنترل روسیه در چهار منطقه اوکراین، و همچنین شبه‌جزیره کریمه که مسکو در سال ۲۰۱۴ آن را به خاک خود ضمیمه کرد، سخن گفته بود.

مذاکرات تازه، پس از دوره‌ای از تنش در روابط بین کی‌یف و واشنگتن بر سر حملات اوکراین به تأسیسات نفتی در اعماق خاک روسیه برگزار می‌شود.

دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا، از اوکراین خواسته بود که این حملات را متوقف کند تا عرضه گازوئیل روسیه به منظور کاهش قیمت جهانی سوخت تسهیل شود.
